properties.name: MEASURED: inside an open batch, a memoised derived scan (detect_gaps; the defect scan, node-type index and adjacency share the memo) answered from before the batch's own writes, because the write generation it is keyed on moved only on a committed write. And a nested begin_batch committed the outer batch early
properties.statement:
Found while building dec:idea-a-refused-typed-write-stores-nothing, 2026-10-02, on main 9ecb405 / d9e2a8f, with failing-first tests in crates/reflow2-core/tests/a_write_unit_is_all_or_nothing.rs, observed FAILING on main.

(1) STALE DERIVED SCAN. Inside DesignGraph::atomically, detect_gaps; add_capability(cap:fresh); detect_gaps returned the first call's gaps, and cap:fresh (asked for by nothing) was absent. The control, the same two calls outside a batch, named cap:fresh. Cause: DerivedMemo is keyed on StorageEngine::write_generation, which ReadCache moved only on invalidate (a committed put/delete, or commit_batch). A buffered write moved nothing, and neither did a discard. Latent in every path that reads a derived scan inside a batch (draw_edges runs typed helper bodies inside atomically).

(2) A NESTED BATCH COMMITTED THE OUTER ONE. begin_batch inside an open batch logged a warning and committed the first. Measured: an outer atomically wrote req:outer, an inner create_nodes failed and discarded, the outer item then failed, and req:outer was durable afterwards. Harmless while no batch sat inside another; fatal to a call-sized unit.

Both fixed in chg:a-refused-write-stores-nothing (staged writes and discards move the generation; batches nest as savepoints).
